title: Annotatio III §.II: Chrysostom samples — immolated Lord handled; teeth fixed in His flesh (Hom. Matt. / Cor. / John)
pass_a_gloss: Among the sayings of the Greek Fathers these of CHRYSOSTOM, most eloquent of the Eastern Fathers, stand out: You will behold, he says, in the sacred Eucharist the Lord immolated. He who sits above with the Father is at that very instant of time handled by the hands of all. You see Him, you touch Him, you eat Him. For I show you neither Angels nor Archangels, but the Lord Himself of them all. In the mysteries blood is drawn from Christ’s side; with this admirable blood the tongue is stained. Hom. 5 & 83 on Matt.; Hom. 24 on 1 Cor. And again: He reduces us into one mass with Himself, and does not permit Himself only to be seen, but also to be touched and eaten and teeth to be fixed in His flesh, so that through the food He has bestowed we are converted into His flesh. Hom. 45 on John.
pass_b_english: Chrysostom (Eastern Fathers’ most eloquent): in the Eucharist you behold the immolated Lord — seated with the Father yet handled, seen, touched, eaten; blood from His side stains the tongue (Hom. Matt. / 1 Cor.).
Again: He knits us into one mass with Himself; teeth are fixed in His flesh so that by the food given we are turned into His flesh (Hom. 45 on John).
source_text: Inter Græcorum Patrum dicta eminent ista CHRYSOSTOMI, Orientalium Patrum disertissimi: Conspicies ait, in sacra Eucharistia Dominum immolatum. Qui cum Patre sursum sedet in illo ipso temporis articulo, omnium manibus pertractatur. Ipsum vides, ipsum tangis, ipsum comedis. Neque enim Angelos neque Archangelos, sed ipsum horum omnium Dominum Tibi ostendo. In mysteriis sanguis ex Christi latere hauritur; hoc admirabili sanguine lingua cruentatur. Hom. 5. & 83. in Matth. Hom. 24. in 1. ad Corinth. Et rursus: Nos in unam secum massam reducit, nec se tantùm videri permittit, sed & tangi & manducari & dentes carni suæ infigi, adeo ut per cibum, quem nobis largitus est, in carnem suam convertamur. Hom. 45. in Johan.
